title: Making Light-Powered Chlamydomonas Bead Bracelets for Teaching Photosynthesis
author: Mautusi Mitra
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgpyjvpw

steps.title: Maintain and Grow Chlamydomonas 4A+ Culture
steps.instruction: Prepare and grow the Chlamydomonas wild type strain 4A+ in TAP media.

substeps.instruction: Maintain 4A+ strain on TAP agar media plates at 25°C in dim light (15-20 µmol m-2s-1).
10-12 days before the activity, inoculate 10 mL of liquid TAP media in a 50 mL flask with cells from a 5-day old TAP agar plate.
After 5 days of growth, add 1 mL of this starter culture to 300 mL of fresh TAP media in a 1L flask.
Grow the culture for 6-7 days at 25°C under continuous illumination of 100 µmol photons m-2s-1 (using 4-6 cool white fluorescent lights) on an open-air orbital shaker at 150-180 rpm.

steps.title: Prepare Alginate and Calcium Chloride Solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary chemical solutions 2 days before bead making.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 2 g of sodium alginate in 100 mL of E-pure water overnight at room temperature, stirring at 500-600 rpm; store at room temperature.
Dissolve 30 g of calcium chloride in 1000 mL of E-pure water and store at 4°C.

steps.title: Determine Cell Density
steps.instruction: Calculate the cell density of the TAP liquid culture to determine the volume needed for harvesting.

substeps.instruction: Count cells using a Hausser Scientific Bright-Line™ Counting Chamber to determine cells per mL.
Calculate the volume required to harvest between 250 x 10^6 and 395 x 10^6 cells per 50 mL falcon tube.

steps.title: Harvest Chlamydomonas Cells
steps.instruction: Concentrate the algae cells via centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Spin down the culture in 50 mL falcon tubes at 1000-1500 g for 3 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and collect the cell pellet (ensure total cells do not exceed 395 x 10^6 per tube).

steps.title: Create Algae-Sodium Alginate Suspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in sodium alginate solution.

substeps.instruction: Add 4-5 mL of 2% sodium alginate to a cell pellet volume of 1.25-1.5 mL (approx. 4:1 or 5:1 ratio) using a P1000 micropipette to reach a final volume of 6-7 mL.
Gently swirl the falcon tubes for 5-10 minutes until the pellet is completely resuspended without clumps; do not vortex.

steps.title: Form Algal Beads
steps.instruction: Drop the suspension into calcium chloride to solidify the beads.

substeps.instruction: Place a beaker of pre-chilled 3% CaCl2 on ice.
Using a P1000 micropipette, steadily add the algae-sodium alginate mix dropwise into the CaCl2. Avoid holding the tip too close to the surface to prevent clogging.
Ensure no air bubbles are in the pipette tip and do not disturb the beaker during pipetting.
Between batches of pipetting, give the CaCl2 beaker a very gentle swirl to harden the beads, then wait for the surface to be still before resuming.
Keep the beads in the chilled CaCl2 on ice for 10-15 minutes for complete solidification.

steps.title: Wash and Store Algal Beads
steps.instruction: Clean the beads of residual salts and store them.

substeps.instruction: Filter the beads from the CaCl2 solution using a strainer or coffee filter (filtered CaCl2 can be stored at 4°C and reused 3-5 times).
Rinse beads thoroughly with tap water for at least 5 minutes to remove residual sodium chloride.
Scoop beads with a plastic spoon into a petri dish containing a small amount of tap water to prevent drying.
Store any leftover beads in tap water in the refrigerator for 2-3 days.

steps.title: Assemble Bracelet and Necklace Hardware
steps.instruction: Prepare the tubing and seals for the jewelry.

substeps.instruction: Cut flexible tubing into 5-inch lengths (bracelets) or 6-inch lengths (necklaces).
Cut the caps off 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and use the tubes to plug the ends of the tubing.
Braid colorful yarns to fit wrist width and loop one braid tightly onto the mouth of each de-capped Eppendorf tube at the ends.
Cut the ends of plastic transfer pipette tips at an angle to create scoops.

steps.title: Fill Tubing with Indicator Solution
steps.instruction: Add water and pH indicator to the tubing.

substeps.instruction: Unplug one end of the tubing.
For bracelets (5-7 inches): Add 3-5 mL of tap water (pH 6.9-7) and 8-9 drops of bicarbonate indicator solution.
For necklaces (6-7 inches): Add 4.5-5.5 mL of tap water and 10-11 drops of bicarbonate indicator solution.
Ensure a 0.5 cm-1 cm air gap remains at each end of the tubing.

steps.title: Load Algae Beads into Tubing
steps.instruction: Insert the beads into the prepared tubing.

substeps.instruction: Use the modified pipette scoop to gently introduce beads into the water (10-12 beads for 5-inch bracelets; 20-35 beads for necklaces).
Let the water flow inside the tubing take the beads from the scoop without squeezing the pipette bulb.
Plug the end of the tubing with the de-capped Eppendorf tube.
Gently swish the tubing to mix the water and indicator, then check for tight seals to prevent leakage.

steps.title: Perform Light and Dark Exposure Experiments
steps.instruction: Observe the pH-driven color changes of the bracelets.

substeps.instruction: Image the bracelet and record the initial pH.
Expose to light (150-200 µmol m-2s-1 using 12-14 cool white fluorescent lights or multiple LED grow lights) for 2-4 hours. The color should change from light red/magenta to dark blue/purple.
Shift to dark for 3-4 hours. The color should change from dark blue/purple to bright yellow.
Repeat the light/dark cycle 2-3 times over 2-3 days.
